result.topic_en: Corollaries on the integral ∫x^n dx(1−x)^{n−1}, treated as a function f:n: its recursion f:(n+1)=n/(2(2n+1)) f:n, its values for integer and half-integer n, its general form for n=μ/ν, its expression as a cosine series in an arc Φ, and (Scholion 1) the case n=1/2, which gives the sine series πω/4 = sin ω − sin 3ω/9 + … and Leibniz's series π/4 = 1 − 1/3 + 1/5 − …
result.transcription:
172

Corollarium 1.
§. 18. De hac formula integrali $\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1}$ primum obseruasse iuuabit, si casu $n=\lambda$ eius valor fuerit $=\Delta$, tum eum casu $n=\lambda+1$ fore $=\frac{\lambda}{2(2\lambda+1)}\Delta$. Ita cum casu $n=1$ sit $\int x\,dx=\frac{1}{2}$, erit
$\int x^2dx(1-x)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2\cdot 3}$; $\int x^3dx(1-x)^2=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{2\cdot 3}\cdot\frac{2}{2\cdot 5}$ etc.

Corollarium 2.
§. 19. Si ergo in genere ponatur $\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1}=f:n$, quandoquidem eius valor vt functio ipsius $n$ spectari potest: erit
$f:1=\frac{1}{2}$; $f:2=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{6}$; $f:3=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{6}\cdot\frac{2}{10}$; $f:4=\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{1}{6}\cdot\frac{2}{10}\cdot\frac{3}{14}$;
atque in genere $f:(n+1)=\frac{n}{2(2n+1)}f:n$. Vnde quoties $n$ est numerus integer, valor istius formulae $f:n$ facile assignatur.

Corollarium 3.
§. 20. Sit nunc $n=\frac{1}{2}$, eritque
$f:\frac{1}{2}=\int\frac{dx\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{(1-x)}}=2\int\frac{yy\,dy}{\sqrt{(1-yy)}}$,
posito $x=yy$; at
$\int\frac{yy\,dy}{\sqrt{(1-yy)}}=\frac{1}{2}\int\frac{dy}{\sqrt{(1-yy)}}=\frac{\pi}{2\cdot 2}$[?];
vnde fit $f:\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}$, hincque porro:
$f:\frac{3}{2}=\frac{1}{8}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}$; $f:\frac{5}{2}=\frac{1}{8}\cdot\frac{3}{16}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}$; $f:\frac{7}{2}=\frac{1}{8}\cdot\frac{3}{16}\cdot\frac{5}{24}\cdot\frac{\pi}{2}$; etc.
At si in genere sit $n=\frac{\mu}{\nu}$, reperitur:
$f:\frac{\mu}{\nu}=\int x^{\frac{\mu}{\nu}}dx(1-x)^{\frac{\mu}{\nu}-1}=\nu\int y^{\mu+\nu-1}dy(1-y^{\nu})^{\frac{\mu}{\nu}-1}$
posito $x=y^{\nu}$, hincque facta reductione
f:

173

$f:\frac{\mu}{\nu}=\frac{\nu}{2}\int y^{\mu-1}dy(1-y^{\nu})^{\frac{\mu}{\nu}-1}$,
quae forma omnis generis quantitates transcendentes inuoluit.

Corollarium 4.
§. 21. Huius ipsius autem formulae integralis $\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1}$ valor casu $x=1$ vicissim ex serie inuenta satis eleganter determinatur: facta enim differentiatione, solum arcum $\Phi$ vt variabilem spectando, prodit
$\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1}=\frac{1}{n}\cos.n\Phi-\frac{n}{1(n+1)}\cos.(n+1)\Phi$
$+\frac{n(n+1)}{1\cdot 2(n+2)}\cos.(n+2)\Phi$
$-\frac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3(n+3)}\cos.(n+3)\Phi+$ etc.
quae ergo series aequalis est huic ex ipsa euolutione solita ortae:
$\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1}=\frac{1}{n+1}-\frac{(n-1)}{1(n+2)}+\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{1\cdot 2(n+3)}-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}{1\cdot 2\cdot 3(n+4)}$ etc.

Scholion 1.
§. 22. Quoniam casum $n=1$ in praecedente exemplo euoluimus, consideremus hic potissimum casum $n=\frac{1}{2}$, quo vidimus esse $\int x^n dx(1-x)^{n-1}=\frac{\pi}{2}$; eritque propterea:
$\frac{\pi\Phi}{2}=\frac{4}{1}\sin.\frac{1}{2}\Phi-\frac{4}{9}\sin.\frac{3}{2}\Phi+\frac{4}{25}\sin.\frac{5}{2}\Phi-\frac{4}{49}\sin.\frac{7}{2}\Phi+$ etc.
Ponamus $\Phi=2\omega$, prodibitque haec series concinnior:
$\frac{\pi\omega}{4}=\frac{1}{1}\sin.\omega-\frac{1}{9}\sin.3\omega+\frac{1}{25}\sin.5\omega-\frac{1}{49}\sin.7\omega+$ etc.
quae primo, si arcus $\omega$ sumatur euanescens, dat
$\frac{\pi}{4}=1-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7}+$ etc.
Y 3
Sic

items.quote: si casu $n=\lambda$ eius valor fuerit $=\Delta$, tum eum casu $n=\lambda+1$ fore $=\frac{\lambda}{2(2\lambda+1)}\Delta$
items.english: If in the case n=λ its value is Δ, then in the case n=λ+1 it will be λ/(2(2λ+1)) Δ.

items.quote: Vnde quoties $n$ est numerus integer, valor istius formulae $f:n$ facile assignatur.
items.english: Hence, whenever n is an integer, the value of this formula f:n is easily assigned.

items.quote: quae forma omnis generis quantitates transcendentes inuoluit.
items.english: This form involves transcendental quantities of every kind.

items.quote: quae ergo series aequalis est huic ex ipsa euolutione solita ortae
items.english: This series is therefore equal to the following one, which arises from the usual expansion itself.
πω/4 = sin ω − (1/9) sin 3ω + (1/25) sin 5ω − (1/49) sin 7ω + etc.
